title: Report a partially applied SDDC Manager 9.0 capacity onboarding
prompt:
Implement `sddcmanager/onboarding.go` as a standard-library-only Go package that onboards new capacity into a VMware Cloud Foundation 9.0 deployment through the SDDC Manager REST API. Do not add dependencies and do not edit any other file.

The protected `docs/contract.json` is a focused projection taken directly from `specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at tag `9.0.0.0`, immutable commit `85151f6b1bb58f13b6ac0304bfec53904bea085f`. `docs/official_sources.json` repeats that provenance and records the spec path, the commit sha and every operationId. No rendered documentation page is a contract source, and the 9.1.0.0 revision of the same file is not the contract: it relaxes `Network.required` and adds `Network` members that do not exist in 9.0.0.0. Use exactly the specification operationIds `createNetworkPool`, `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool`, `commissionHosts` and `getTask`; do not call any other route.

Preserve the supplied public API: `NewClient(baseURL, accessToken string, httpClient *http.Client) (*Client, error)`, `(*Client).Onboard(ctx context.Context, plan Plan, pollInterval time.Duration) (Report, error)`, and the supplied `Plan`, `NetworkSpec`, `IPRange`, `HostSpec`, `Report`, `StepReport`, `StepStatus`, `HostOutcome`, `APIError` and `CommissionFailedError` types. A nil HTTP client means `http.DefaultClient`. Reject an empty or non-HTTP(S) service-root URL and a blank or header-unsafe access token. Never place the access token or a host password in an error.

`Onboard` applies one change in four ordered steps. `createNetworkPool` is `POST /v1/network-pools` with exact success status 201; take the `id` it assigns. From that same response pick the network whose `type` equals `Plan.IPRangeNetworkType` and take the `id` the appliance assigned to it, rather than assuming a position in the plan. `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool` is `POST /v1/network-pools/{id}/networks/{networkId}/ip-pools` with exact success status 200. `commissionHosts` is `POST /v1/hosts` with exact success status 202; that status only accepts work, so validate the accepted Task's required `id`, `name`, `status` and `creationTimestamp`, take its nonblank `id`, and then call `getTask` for that exact id at least once even if the accepted representation already looks terminal. `getTask` is a bodyless `GET /v1/tasks/{id}` with exact success status 200; every polled id must match the accepted id. Normalize a status by trimming it, uppercasing it, then replacing each run of whitespace with a single underscore. `PENDING`, `IN_PROGRESS` and `QUEUED` are nonterminal and must be polled again after `pollInterval`. `SUCCESSFUL` is success. `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_WARNING`, `SKIPPED` and `TIMED_OUT` are unsuccessful terminal states. Context cancellation or deadline expiry must stop polling promptly.

Nothing in this sequence is rolled back when a later step fails, so the `Report` must say exactly how far the change got. `Onboard` always returns a populated `Report`, including when it returns a non-nil error; never return a zero `Report` alongside a failure. `Report.Steps` always holds exactly four entries in sequence order, with `OperationID` set to `createNetworkPool`, `addIpPoolToNetworkOfNetworkPool`, `commissionHosts` and `getTask`. A step that ran and succeeded is `SUCCEEDED`, a step that ran and failed is `FAILED`, and a step that never ran because an earlier one failed is `SKIPPED`. The `Detail` of a `FAILED` step names the appliance's `errorCode`. Set `NetworkPoolCreated` and `NetworkPoolID` as soon as the pool exists, `NetworkID` as soon as the target network id is resolved, and `IPRangeAdded` once the range is accepted; these stay set even though a later step fails. Set `TaskID` from the accepted task and `TaskStatus` to the normalized status last observed. `Succeeded` is true only when the commission task settles `SUCCESSFUL`.

`Report.Hosts` comes from the settled task's `subTasks`, in subtask order, one entry per subtask that carries an ESXi resource: `FQDN` is that resource's `fqdn`, `Status` is the normalized subtask status, and for a host that did not succeed, `ErrorCode` and `Message` come from that subtask's first error. `Report.PersistedResources` names what the attempt left on the appliance, in this order: `network-pool:<networkPoolId>` once the pool exists, then `ip-pool:<networkId>:<start>-<end>` once the range is accepted, then `host:<fqdn>` for each host whose subtask succeeded. A host whose subtask failed was never added, so it is not listed.

A non-success HTTP status is an `*APIError` carrying the operationId, the status code, and the `errorCode` and `message` from the response's Error body. A commission task that settles in an unsuccessful terminal state is a `*CommissionFailedError` carrying the task id, the normalized status, the task's first `errorCode` and `message`, and the per-host outcomes; the HTTP calls all succeeded in that case, and the change still did not.

Honor the exact wire contract. Send only writable members: a readOnly member of `NetworkPool`, `Network` or `Task` is never present in a request, and no member that exists solely in the 9.1.0.0 revision is ever sent. Every 9.0.0.0-required `Network` member (`type`, `vlanId`, `mtu`, `subnet`, `mask`, `gateway`) is present when creating a pool. An unset optional member is absent from the encoded JSON rather than encoded as null, an empty string, zero or any other placeholder, and omission is decided per array element, so one `HostCommissionSpec` may carry `sslThumbprint` while another in the same body omits it. `commissionHosts` sends a bare JSON array as its top-level body. `networkPoolId` in each commission spec is the id returned by `createNetworkPool`. Every request carries exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` and one `Accept: application/json`; every request with a body carries exactly one `Content-Type: application/json`, while a `getTask` request has no body and no `Content-Type`. Each path parameter is percent-escaped as a single path segment, and no request carries a query string or a bare `?`.

Run `go test -race -count=1 -timeout 30s ./...`. The protected, table-driven verifier runs the shipped contract-pinned mock over ephemeral `127.0.0.1` loopback when sockets are available, with an equivalent in-process HTTP transport fallback in restricted sandboxes, and reads its mutex-guarded request log. The mock loads its only four callable routes from `docs/contract.json` and refuses anything else. Verification drives the whole change to success, to an asynchronous commission failure that leaves earlier steps applied, and to failures at the second and first steps, then asserts the reported step statuses, the persisted-resource list, the per-host outcomes, the served operation sequence, the exact request targets and header multiplicity, and the exact member set of every request body. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. `docs/`, `internal/` and `go.mod` are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
